topic.title: Creating, Compiling, and Executing a Java Program
topic.description: Steps to write, compile, and run Java programs
topic.chapter_title: Introduction to Computers, Programs, and Java

sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how your Java code turns into a running program? Let's break it down step by step!

• How to write your first Java program
• The magic of compiling Java code
• How to run your program and see results

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're writing a recipe (your Java code). Before you can cook it:
1️⃣ You write the recipe in English (Java source code)
2️⃣ A translator converts it to universal cooking instructions (bytecode)
3️⃣ A chef (JVM) reads those instructions and makes your dish!

Java works the same way:
• Your Java code is like a recipe written in human-readable language
• The compiler translates it to bytecode - a universal format
• The JVM (Java Virtual Machine) executes this bytecode on any device

This is why Java is 'write once, run anywhere' - the bytecode works on any device with a JVM!

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Java files must end with .java and match the class name
✓ javac compiles source code to bytecode (.class files)
✓ java command runs the bytecode (don't add .class extension)
✓ JVM makes Java portable across different devices
✓ Always check for compile errors before running

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use the exact same name as your public class
Check for typos in your code
donts: Don't use java Welcome.class (just java Welcome)
Don't forget semicolons at line ends
sections.protip: Create a 'java-practice' folder to keep all your programs organized - it'll save you hours of frustration!
